did_you_know.text: Did you know? Jehoash became king of Judah when he was only seven years old—one of the youngest ages at which a king is described as ascending the throne in the Bible.
Did you know? Jehoash reigned in Jerusalem for forty years, and his mother’s name was Zibiah of Beersheba.

Did you know? The text says that Jehoash did what was right in the eyes of the LORD all his days while Jehoiada the priest instructed him; nevertheless, the high places were not removed, and the people continued to sacrifice and burn incense there.
Did you know? Jehoash designated the sacred funds and the offerings for repairing the damage to the Temple, but the priests failed to carry out the repairs for many years.
Did you know? In the twenty-third year of Jehoash’s reign, it became clear that the priests still had not repaired the damage to the Temple, so the king changed the way the funds were collected.
Did you know? The solution was to place a chest with an opening beside the altar, so that the priests could put all the money brought to the house of the LORD into it.
Did you know? The money collected in the chest was counted under the joint supervision of the royal secretary and the high priest, creating an organized system for overseeing the Temple funds.
Did you know? The contribution money was used to pay craftsmen and to purchase timber and quarried stone for strengthening and repairing the Temple.
Did you know? The money from the guilt offerings and sin offerings was not put into the repair fund; according to the text, it remained in the hands of the priests.

Did you know? After Hazael king of Aram captured Gath and turned toward Jerusalem, Jehoash gave him the sacred treasures and the gold from the treasuries of the house of the LORD and the royal palace, and as a result Hazael withdrew from Jerusalem.
